segments.title: One key press
sentences: This is a landing page with no hero image.
No feature grid. No testimonial wall.
There is a terminal, and a command waiting inside it.
You press Enter once.
Then the product explains itself.
segments.notes: Open on the real page. Hold the terminal. The command ghost blinks. Push in as the key is pressed.

segments.title: The contract
sentences: The demo has exactly one interaction.
Press Enter, or click Run.
That is the whole contract.
No carousel. No scroll trick. No second ask.
Everything after the key press is a consequence.
segments.notes: One key icon in the centre, a ripple, and the rest of the page furniture falling away.

segments.title: The stage
sentences: The terminal is the hero.
Near-black glass, phosphor lime, scanlines, a soft vignette.
It looks like the place where work actually happens.
The command types itself into the prompt.
Attention stays on the line that matters.
segments.notes: Terminal screenshot as an object. Callout lines to glass, scanline, prompt and caret.

segments.title: Four checks
sentences: The run is four checks.
Types, lint, tests, build.
Each row waits, turns amber while it works, then goes green.
The detail line narrates the messy middle.
Errors found. Patches applied. Tests passing.
The result is a receipt.
segments.notes: Four rows build in sequence. Real labels, real counts, real fixes. Amber working, green fixed.

segments.title: The body
sentences: The work needs a body.
Each check gets a small robot on a canvas above the terminal.
It spawns from the caret and follows a curved path to its row.
It blinks, sparks, then pops a checkmark.
The robot makes the latency legible.
segments.notes: Draw the Bezier path from caret to row, then the robot on it. Spark and checkmark on the last beat.

segments.title: The clock
sentences: Under the animation, one clock runs everything.
Every pause waits on a frame-driven queue.
One animation frame advances the timeline and the canvas together.
Hide the tab, or scroll away, and the run pauses.
The demo never races ahead of you.
segments.notes: One RAF pulse feeding two lanes: timeline and canvas. A visibility gate closes and both lanes hold.

segments.title: The quiet layer
sentences: Sound arrives only after you press Enter.
A tiny synthesizer builds every sound from oscillators and filtered noise.
Key clicks, spawn blips, spark ticks, a ping for each green check.
No audio files. No autoplay. No surprise.
Mute it, and the run keeps its rhythm on screen.
segments.notes: Audio graph left to right: source, filter, gain, compressor, destination. Notes appear as events.

segments.title: The compression
sentences: The terminal says two minutes and fourteen seconds.
The choreography is compressed to about ten.
That is a lie about time, not about sequence.
The state machine is real even when the work is scripted.
Point it at a live feed, and it becomes a product.
segments.notes: Two clocks: 2:14 and 0:10. Task data object. A live feed arrow replaces the scripted array.

segments.title: The quiet defaults
sentences: The page still works when the motion stops.
Reduced motion hides the canvas and keeps every status change.
Enter starts a run. Every control is a real button.
The layout holds from laptop to phone.
Restraint is part of the design, not a fallback.
segments.notes: Split stage: full motion and reduced motion, same status rows. Keyboard and responsive outlines.

segments.title: The demo is the product
sentences: One key press.
Four checks.
Twelve fixes.
A branch ready to push.
And the next run is one key away.
The demo is the product.
segments.notes: Return to the complete terminal, then pull back to the whole page. The final line stands alone.
